dialogue.content: こんばんは、時間になったら始めますのでよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Good evening. We'll begin at the scheduled time. Thank you for being here.

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、どうぞよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: The pleasure is mine. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: 本日はご相談ありがとうございます。はじめに年齢、性別、ご相談内容をお聞かせください。
dialogue.English: Thank you for reaching out today. To start, may I ask your age, gender, and the nature of your concern?

dialogue.content: 43歳、女性です。16歳の息子について相談です。
dialogue.English: I'm a 43-year-old woman. I'm here to talk about my 16-year-old son.

dialogue.content: お聞かせくださいましてありがとうございます息子さんについてですね。よろしければもう少し詳しくお話を聞かせてもらえますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. So, it's about your son. If you're comfortable, could you tell me a little more about it?

dialogue.content: 幼い頃から育てにくさを感じることがあり、恐らく自閉の傾向も少しあるかと思うのですが、ふつうの学校生活に馴染めず、高校は通信制の学校を選びました。
dialogue.English: I've felt that he's been difficult to raise since he was little, and I suspect he might have some autistic tendencies. He couldn't fit into a regular school environment, so for high school, we chose a correspondence school.

dialogue.content: 外に出て人と関わると物凄く疲れるようで、小中の頃は学校から帰宅後、そのまま２時間くらい寝てしまったり。
dialogue.English: It seems that going out and interacting with people exhausts him. During elementary and middle school, he would often come home from school and sleep for about two hours straight.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。普通の学校に馴染めないとご不安にもなりますよね。自閉の傾向があるとの事でしたが、いつごろから気になりま始めましたか？
dialogue.English: I see. It must be worrying when he can't fit into a regular school. You mentioned he might have autistic tendencies; when did you start to notice that?

dialogue.content: すみません、行違いましたね、
dialogue.English: My apologies, it seems our messages crossed.

dialogue.content: １歳とかそれくらいのときも、人見知り場所見知りが激しく、子育て支援センターなどに行っても泣きわめいてばかりなので、私の方が居づらくなってしまうような感じでした。
dialogue.English: Even around age one, he had severe stranger and place anxiety. When we went to child-rearing support centers, he would just cry and scream, which made it difficult for me to stay there.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。それはお辛かったと思います。そういう時、あなたはどう対処されてきたのですか？
dialogue.English: I see. That must have been tough. How have you been coping with situations like that?

dialogue.content: 核家族なので、なるべく人との接触をと思い、週に一度は通うようにしていて、泣いても部屋の端で落ち着くのを待って、本人が気の向くものだけで遊ばせるような感じでした。
dialogue.English: We're a nuclear family, so I thought it was important for him to have contact with others. I tried to take him there once a week, and even if he cried, I would wait for him to calm down in a corner of the room and let him play with whatever he was interested in.

dialogue.content: みんなで体操とかは、絶対やろうとしませんでしたね。
dialogue.English: He would absolutely refuse to do group activities like exercises.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね、息子さんにも周りにも気を使われて、あなたもお辛かったですね。それから
dialogue.English: I see. You were considerate of both your son and those around you, which must have been hard on you as well. And then...

dialogue.content: 小中学校は、人にも馴染めず、ずっとご不安を抱えていらっしゃるのですね
dialogue.English: So in elementary and junior high he couldn’t fit in with others, and you’ve been carrying these ongoing worries, is that right?

dialogue.content: ちなみに息子さんは家ではどんな感じですか？
dialogue.English: By the way, what is your son like at home?

dialogue.content: 私にはそうでもないのですが、父親に対しては何か自分と対等というような感じで、すごく反抗的なものの言い方をします。
dialogue.English: He's not really like that with me, but with his father, he speaks in a very rebellious way, as if they're equals.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。反抗的になってきたのはいつごろからですか？
dialogue.English: I see. When did he start becoming rebellious?

dialogue.content: 外で感情をうまく出せないので
dialogue.English: Because he can’t express his emotions well outside—

dialogue.content: 家でそういうふうになるのかなと思っていますが、、、
dialogue.English: so I think that might be why he acts that way at home, but...

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。息子さんは高校1年生ですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Is your son in his first year of high school?

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 反抗するようになったのはここ最近ですか？
dialogue.English: Has the rebellion started recently?

dialogue.content: 父親に対しての物言いは、小学生の頃からそういう傾向はありました。
dialogue.English: He's had a tendency to speak that way to his father since elementary school.

dialogue.content: そうでしたか・・・。夫さんはそれに対してどう対応されいてるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see... How does your husband respond to that?

dialogue.content: 怒ることをしない人なので、冷静に対応してますね。私がそばにいる時は、「どう思う？」と笑いながら聞いてきたりします。
dialogue.English: He's not one to get angry, so he responds calmly. When I'm around, he sometimes asks me with a smile, "What do you think?"

dialogue.content: それを聞いて安心しました。優しい夫さんですね。反抗期は早い子だったら小学校高学年から、また普通でも中学、高校とどの家庭でも当たり前のように訪れるので、当たり前のように普通に成長しているのかな？と思いますが、いかがですか？
dialogue.English: I'm relieved to hear that. He sounds like a kind husband. The rebellious phase is a normal part of growing up for any family, starting as early as upper elementary school for some, or usually in middle or high school. So, I wonder if he's just growing up normally? What are your thoughts?

dialogue.content: 二人の関係は、それはそれでいいのですが、今後息子の将来について、やはり心配です。ふつうに就職するのは難しいのではないかと感じます。
dialogue.English: Their relationship is fine as it is, but I'm still worried about my son's future. I feel it might be difficult for him to get a regular job.

dialogue.content: そうですね、親としては将来が気になってしまいますよね。息子さんは、自閉の傾向があると最初にお伺いしましたが、
dialogue.English: Yes, as a parent, it's natural to be concerned about the future. You mentioned at the beginning that your son has autistic tendencies...

dialogue.content: 今、通信制の高校だという事で、学業の方ではどんな感じですか？
dialogue.English: Given that he's in a correspondence high school now, how is he doing with his studies?

dialogue.content: 勉強は基本的に好きではないですね。成績も良くないです。
dialogue.English: He basically doesn't like studying. His grades aren't good either.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。ちなみに息子さんはご兄弟はいますか？
dialogue.English: I see. By the way, does your son have any siblings?

dialogue.content: 自分が興味のあることに対しては知識がすごいのですが、関心のないことに関して、努力ができないようですね。一人っ子です。
dialogue.English: He has amazing knowledge about things he's interested in, but he can't seem to put in the effort for things that don't interest him. He's an only child.

dialogue.content: 色々聞かせていただいてありがとうございます。今までお話を聞いた中で、あなたが一番悩む（気になる）ことは何でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing all of this with me. From everything you've told me, what is the one thing that worries (or concerns) you the most?

dialogue.content: このままだと、いわゆるニートのようにならないか心配です。通信制で時間があるので、バイトを始めてみたのですが、学校の課題が遅れまくり、父親が辞めさせました。
dialogue.English: I'm worried that if things continue like this, he'll become what they call a NEET. Since he has a lot of time with correspondence school, he tried getting a part-time job, but he fell way behind on his school assignments, so his father made him quit.

dialogue.content: 私としては、バイトと課題の提出が遅れたことは別問題だと思うのですが
dialogue.English: From my perspective, I think the part-time job and the late assignments are separate issues, but...

dialogue.content: バイトが終ると疲れてしまうようで、帰ってバタンキューのような状態で。
dialogue.English: After his shifts he seems exhausted—he comes home and just crashes.

dialogue.content: どう社会に対応させるか、悩みます。
dialogue.English: I’m struggling with how to help him adapt to society.

dialogue.content: 息子さんの将来、疲れて帰ると寝てしまって身体の事が心配なのですね
dialogue.English: So you're concerned about your son's future, and also about his health when he comes home exhausted and just falls asleep, is that right?

dialogue.content: そうですよね。親であれば心配になる事は当然のことだと思います。でも
dialogue.English: I understand. It's completely natural for a parent to worry. However...

dialogue.content: 息子さんは興味があることに対しては知識がすごいとのことでしたので、まだお若いのですから、どんなことに興味があるか、これから探していくのもいいのではないのでしょうか？それを
dialogue.English: You mentioned he has tremendous knowledge about his interests, and since he’s still young, it might be a good idea to explore what he’s interested in from now on. That...

dialogue.content: 職業につなげていく方もたくさんいらっしゃいます
dialogue.English: There are many people who turn their interests into a career.

dialogue.content: お身体の方もご心配かとおもいますが、病院などに相談されたことはありますか？
dialogue.English: I imagine you're also concerned about his physical health. Have you ever consulted a doctor or a hospital about it?

dialogue.content: 起立性障害の傾向があるとは言われましたが、市の発達支援センターで検査を受けても、いわゆるグレーゾーンの範疇で、今後どうという支援の方針もありませんでした。
dialogue.English: I was told he has a tendency for orthostatic dysregulation, but even after getting tested at the city's developmental support center, he fell into the so-called "gray zone," and there was no clear support plan for the future.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。今後の事で支援方針がなかったとのことでしたらご不安になりますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. It must be unsettling to not have a support plan for the future.

dialogue.content: 第一には本人に寄り添うことなんでしょうが、自立させるためにどうしたらよいのかと悩みます。
dialogue.English: I know the first priority is to be there for him, but I struggle with how to help him become independent.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。夫さんにも相談されたりすると思いますが、夫さんはどうお考えですか？
dialogue.English: I understand. I imagine you talk with your husband about this as well. What are his thoughts?

dialogue.content: 仕方ない、と言っています。いつまでも自分が面倒をみれる訳ではないのに。
dialogue.English: He says, "It can't be helped," even though he won't be able to look after him forever.

dialogue.content: 仕方ないと言われると、ますます不安になりますよね。少し私からお話しさせていただきたいのですが
dialogue.English: Being told "it can't be helped" must make you even more anxious. There's something I'd like to share with you, if I may.

dialogue.content: 将来の事は誰も予想できませんまだ、息子さんはお若いので、色んな可能性を秘めていると思います。人との関り方が苦手、就職ができないかもしれないと、
dialogue.English: No one can predict the future. Your son is still young, and I believe he has many possibilities. I know you're worried that he finds it hard to relate to people and may have difficulty finding employment...

dialogue.content: 不安で仕方ないと思いますが、今、そういった方の就職斡旋などしてくれる所も増えてきています
dialogue.English: I understand it’s hard not to worry, but nowadays, there are an increasing number of places that offer job placement support for people in his situation.

dialogue.content: そうですね
dialogue.English: That's true.

dialogue.content: あなたもきっと、悩んで心にゆとりがないのではないかと感じます。まずはあなたがゆっくりと休んで、改めてご家族でこれからの事を考えていくことも必要かなと思いますがいかがですか？
dialogue.English: I sense that you must be so worried that you have little peace of mind. Perhaps it's important for you to first take a good rest, and then as a family, you can think about the future again. What do you think?

dialogue.content: （お時間すぎてしまい申し訳ありません）
dialogue.English: (My apologies for going over our time.)

dialogue.content: 私も今は、これは基本的には彼自身の問題、と捉えているので、そんなに息子のことばかり考えているわけではないですが、
dialogue.English: Right now, I see this as fundamentally his own issue, so it's not like I'm constantly thinking only about my son, but...

dialogue.content: そうですね、あまり深刻に考えないようにしたいと思います。
dialogue.English: You're right. I will try not to dwell on it too much.

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、お時間すみません。。
dialogue.English: No, I’m the one who should apologize for taking up your time.

dialogue.content: はい、もちろん息子さんも大切ですが、あなたもご自愛いただければと思います。お話の途中ですがいったんこれで終了させていただきます。また、何かありましたらいつでも相談しにきてください。本日はありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Yes, of course your son is important, but I hope you will also take care of yourself. I know we're in the middle of our conversation, but we'll have to end here for today. Please feel free to come back and talk anytime if anything comes up. Thank you very much for today.

dialogue.content: どうもありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: （長々とすみません。遅い時間までありがとうございました。お時間ある時に評価いただければ幸いです。）
dialogue.English: (I apologize for taking so much of your time. Thank you for staying so late. I would appreciate it if you could leave a review when you have a moment.)

dialogue.content: （またご縁がありましたらよろしくお願いいたします。では、失礼します。）
dialogue.English: (I hope to have the opportunity to speak with you again. Well then, goodbye.)
